title: This look distinctive or just weird?
author: Axel0009
selftext:
I’m making a short psychological horror game, and I’ve been trying to give it a distinct visual style, something that doesn’t immediately make people think AI slop.

But I’ve spent so long staring at the same graphics that I can’t tell anymore whether the style is working or just looks odd.

What’s your first impression?

comments.author: Federal_Bluebird_487
comments.body: Muddy is the best way I can describe it. To me in the darkest places its like when your eyes are trying to adjust to the light different but its just not working so its jarring to look at. Maybe thats what you were going for idk but it muddies my vision looking at the darkest areas(not so much present in the kitchen area with more lighting)

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body: odd and too dark , could prob try out grey scales / b&w

comments.author: ontagi
comments.body: Kinda reminds me of lethal company, would lift the shadows a bit. It's mostly unique and doesn't look bad, nothing wrong with going for your own artstyle.

comments.author: NightMailworks
comments.body: I would try applying surface-stable dithering like described here: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HPqGaIMVuLs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HPqGaIMVuLs)

comments.author: bboingy
comments.body: epic

comments.author: TopTippityTop
comments.body: It would get tiring, imo

comments.author: JTxt
comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/hlek0g30k41i1.png

looks like a posterize on the three channels, making some interesting colors in the blend, feels like rendering on old computers.   I think it's interesting.  Not sure what feel you're going for though.  
I've done something kind of similar, that may give some ideas.  I blured to soften the details, greyscale and posterized to seprate into value shapes, then a blured color overlay back over it. (Like in this interactive shader tool I'm working on. [https://jtxt.org/tools/squint-check/](https://jtxt.org/tools/squint-check/) )

comments.author: _Fauxpaw
comments.body: Reminds me of an art style for a game I can't recall. I like it.

comments.author: Jayston1994
comments.body: I love it

comments.author: Just-Routine967
comments.body:
The banding is a bit too strong for me.

I think it could look really cool with some adjustment and with it showing on npcs too.

comments.author: OvernightTechnology
comments.body: Looks really good. Fits the genre I guess. As suggested here: try out black/white/gray - but maybe only in certain moments in the story. But you might already have that going on. Keep on going!

comments.author: zavtraleto
comments.body: Looks good, but sloppy to me - place assets properly at least. Visually it’s ripoff of a game about working on a kitchen

comments.author: AsobismEN
comments.body: I like it, especially the way the light ripples out! One idea could be potentially a colder colour palette in the shadows and then warmer in the lights to combat the "muddiness" as others have called it, and draw attention to how cool that part of the shader is.

comments.author: NoBackupDev
comments.body: The look itself is good. Low bit colors are a tried and tested look. What will make it distinctive is the personality which will come through the models and textures.

comments.author: cheyumaama
comments.body: Distinctive, but make the chick better bro

comments.author: EmberAndAshTheCradle
comments.body: I like the looking of it, only the light sources boder me a little (too much "light" on the surfaces)

comments.author: Sorrytokeepyouwaitin
comments.body: Looks weird but in a good way. I actually really dig it. Reminds me of certain pc games from mid 90s they had a texture similar to your wall texture

comments.author: santigv1500
comments.body: it gives me some beholder 3d vibes. btw i think the ligth and shadows looks a little bit odd, i would work more on that aspect

comments.author: OneMoreFightGame
comments.body:
I think the blended coloration is a good style and things do look distinct enough in this that visual clarity doesn't feel lost overall (especially in the lighter area). It also feels eerie because the style makes it "feel" like something could be lurking in the peripheral

But the initial shot does seem quite dark and the shadows could be problematic if it's not intended to take a lot of focus to see. Truthfully, I think we'd need to see a good amount more to know if the visual style would grate at you over time or not

comments.author: Lambisexual
comments.body: Looks good, although the character model doesn't
